# Purpose

This notebook gets the USAJOBS job announcement data the RC/RQ team uses and runs the analyses
classifiers, IOs and pod leads have asked for in the project trainings and check-ins:

| # | Analysis | Why the team needs it |
|---|----------|----------------------|
| A | **Series synopsis** (postings, agencies, organizational titles, grade range, pay plan, hiring paths) | The "USA Jobs synopsis" that goes into each series taxonomy (organizational titles, grade coverage, recruitment activity). |
| B | **Grade distribution and concentration** | Shows which grades agencies actually recruit at (e.g. the 0661 "majority above GS-5" question). It supports grade-level illustrations alongside EHRI. |
| C | **Agency drill-down and pay system comparison** | Compares VA (Title 38 / hybrid) with Title 5 agencies on grade and pay (0661, 0667, 0671). |
| D | **Year comparison 2024 vs 2025 vs 2026** | 2024 is the pre-freeze baseline and 2025 is used as a comparison year. |
| E | **Keyword evidence search** ("needle in the haystack") | Checks whether an AI redline recommendation (e.g. "property disposal", "e-discovery") shows up in real announcements, and how often and at which grades. |
| F | **Competencies agencies list** | Gives evidence for general **and technical** competencies, which matters most where OPM has no validated technical model. |
| G | **Emerging and declining duty language plus technology/automation terms** | Feeds the "Impact of Automation" section and shows how the work is changing. |
| H | **Education requirement signals** | Supports the skills-based hiring shift (EO 14170 / Chance to Compete / Merit Hiring Plan). |

**Data source.** The USAJOBS Historic JOA API (`/api/historicjoa`, the metadata) and
`/api/historicjoa/announcementtext` (the full text). Both endpoints are public. If you've been given a key
(Xavier's setup), set `USAJOBS_API_KEY` and it is sent as `Authorization-Key`. The pulls run in
parallel by series and month, so no single request chain gets near the volume cap.

**Workflow.** Run locally in RStudio or VS Code against flat files. Outputs go to `params$out_dir`. Then copy
`out_dir/sharepoint/USA Jobs <year> data/` into the RCRQ data folder on SharePoint.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 6)
```

# 1. API helpers

All network access goes through `get_json()`. Paging follows the `paging$next` link until the API
stops returning a continuation token.

```{r api-helpers}
BASE_URL <- "https://data.usajobs.gov"
ENDPOINTS <- c(joa = "/api/historicjoa", text = "/api/historicjoa/announcementtext")

get_json <- function(url) {
  req <- request(url) |>
    req_user_agent(Sys.getenv("USAJOBS_USER_AGENT", "opm-rcrq-analysis")) |>
    req_timeout(180) |>
    req_retry(max_tries = 6,
              is_transient = \(r) resp_status(r) %in% c(429, 500, 502, 503, 504),
              backoff = \(i) min(60, 2^i))
  key <- Sys.getenv("USAJOBS_API_KEY", "")
  if (nzchar(key)) req <- req_headers(req, `Authorization-Key` = key)
  resp <- req_perform(req)
  fromJSON(resp_body_string(resp), simplifyVector = TRUE, flatten = FALSE)
}

build_url <- function(endpoint, query) {
  q <- paste(names(query), vapply(query, \(v) URLencode(as.character(v), reserved = TRUE), ""),
             sep = "=", collapse = "&")
  paste0(BASE_URL, endpoint, "?", q)
}

# Collapse a list-column of small data frames (jobCategories, hiringPaths, positionLocations) to text
collapse_nested <- function(col, fields, sep = "|") {
  if (is.null(col)) return(NA_character_)
  vapply(col, function(x) {
    if (!is.data.frame(x) || nrow(x) == 0) return(NA_character_)
    x <- x[, intersect(fields, names(x)), drop = FALSE]
    if (!ncol(x)) return(NA_character_)
    paste(unique(do.call(paste, c(x, sep = ", "))), collapse = sep)
  }, character(1))
}

# Make one page of results a flat, all-character tibble so pages always bind cleanly
flatten_page <- function(df) {
  if (is.null(df) || !length(df) || !nrow(df)) return(tibble())
  df <- as_tibble(df)
  if ("jobCategories" %in% names(df))
    df$series_list <- collapse_nested(df$jobCategories, "series")
  if ("hiringPaths" %in% names(df))
    df$hiring_paths <- collapse_nested(df$hiringPaths, "hiringPath")
  if ("positionLocations" %in% names(df)) {
    df$locations   <- collapse_nested(df$positionLocations,
                                      c("positionLocationCity", "positionLocationState"), " | ")
    df$n_locations <- vapply(df$positionLocations,
                             \(x) if (is.data.frame(x)) nrow(x) else 0L, integer(1))
  }
  df |>
    select(where(\(x) !is.list(x))) |>
    mutate(across(everything(), as.character))
}

fetch_all <- function(endpoint, query, throttle = params$throttle) {
  url <- build_url(endpoint, query)
  pages <- list()
  repeat {
    js <- get_json(url)
    pages[[length(pages) + 1]] <- flatten_page(js$data)
    nxt <- js$paging$`next`
    tok <- js$paging$metadata$continuationToken
    if (is.null(nxt) || !nzchar(nxt) || is.null(tok) || NROW(js$data) == 0) break
    url <- paste0(BASE_URL, nxt)
    Sys.sleep(throttle)
  }
  bind_rows(pages)
}
```

# 2. Pull the data (parallel, cached)

One unit of work is **endpoint × series × month**. Each unit is saved as its own `.rds`, so an
interrupted run picks up where it stopped.

```{r pull-plan}
month_windows <- function(years) {
  starts <- seq(as.Date(paste0(min(years), "-01-01")),
                as.Date(paste0(max(years), "-12-01")), by = "month")
  starts <- starts[as.integer(format(starts, "%Y")) %in% years & starts <= Sys.Date()]
  ends <- do.call(c, lapply(starts, \(s) seq(s, by = "month", length.out = 2)[2] - 1))
  tibble(start = starts, end = pmin(ends, Sys.Date()))
}

endpoints_to_pull <- if (isTRUE(params$pull_text)) c("joa", "text") else "joa"
plan_tbl <- tidyr::expand_grid(endpoint = endpoints_to_pull, series = SERIES,
                               month_windows(YEARS)) |>
  mutate(file = file.path(RAW_DIR, endpoint,
                          sprintf("%s_%s.rds", series, format(start, "%Y-%m"))),
         is_current = format(start, "%Y-%m") == format(Sys.Date(), "%Y-%m"),
         todo = params$refresh | is_current | !file.exists(file))

plan_tbl |> count(endpoint, todo)
```

```{r pull-run}
pull_one <- function(endpoint, series, start, end, file, ...) {
  out <- tryCatch({
    df <- fetch_all(ENDPOINTS[[endpoint]],
                    list(PositionSeries = series,
                         StartPositionOpenDate = format(start),
                         EndPositionOpenDate   = format(end)))
    df$pull_series <- series
    saveRDS(df, file)
    tibble(rows = nrow(df), error = NA_character_)
  }, error = \(e) tibble(rows = NA_integer_, error = conditionMessage(e)))
  bind_cols(tibble(endpoint, series, start), out)
}

todo <- filter(plan_tbl, todo)
if (nrow(todo)) {
  future::plan(future::multisession, workers = params$workers)
  pull_log <- furrr::future_pmap_dfr(
    select(todo, endpoint, series, start, end, file), pull_one,
    .options = furrr::furrr_options(seed = TRUE), .progress = TRUE)
  future::plan(future::sequential)
  write_csv(pull_log, file.path(OUT, sprintf("pull_log_%s.csv", format(Sys.time(), "%Y%m%d_%H%M"))))
  pull_log |> summarise(units = n(), rows = sum(rows, na.rm = TRUE), errors = sum(!is.na(error)))
} else {
  message("Everything is cached. Set params$refresh = TRUE to re-pull.")
}
```

```{r pull-errors}
# Any failures? Re-run the chunk above; only the missing units are pulled again.
if (exists("pull_log")) filter(pull_log, !is.na(error))
```

# 3. Combine & clean

```{r combine}
read_cached <- function(endpoint) {
  files <- list.files(file.path(RAW_DIR, endpoint), pattern = "\\.rds$", full.names = TRUE)
  keep  <- sub("_.*$", "", basename(files)) %in% SERIES
  bind_rows(lapply(files[keep], readRDS))
}

to_num <- \(x) suppressWarnings(as.numeric(x))
strip_html <- function(x) {
  x |>
    str_replace_all("<[^>]+>", " ") |>
    str_replace_all("&nbsp;|&#160;", " ") |>
    str_replace_all("&amp;", "&") |>
    str_replace_all("&lt;", "<") |>
    str_replace_all("&gt;", ">") |>
    str_replace_all("&#39;|&rsquo;", "'") |>
    str_squish()
}

joa_raw <- read_cached("joa")

joa <- joa_raw |>
  distinct(usajobsControlNumber, pull_series, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  mutate(
    series      = pull_series,
    open_date   = as.Date(substr(positionOpenDate, 1, 10)),
    close_date  = as.Date(substr(positionCloseDate, 1, 10)),
    year        = as.integer(format(open_date, "%Y")),
    month       = as.Date(format(open_date, "%Y-%m-01")),
    grade_min   = as.integer(to_num(minimumGrade)),
    grade_max   = as.integer(to_num(maximumGrade)),
    fpl         = as.integer(to_num(promotionPotential)),
    hourly      = str_detect(coalesce(salaryType, ""), regex("hour", ignore_case = TRUE)),
    salary_min  = to_num(minimumSalary) * if_else(hourly, 2087, 1),
    salary_max  = to_num(maximumSalary) * if_else(hourly, 2087, 1),
    openings_n  = to_num(totalOpenings),          # often "Few"/"Many" -> NA
    is_va       = coalesce(hiringDepartmentCode == "VA", FALSE) |
                  str_detect(coalesce(hiringDepartmentName, ""), "Veterans Affairs"),
    is_supv     = str_detect(coalesce(supervisoryStatus, ""), regex("^y", ignore_case = TRUE)),
    multi_series = str_detect(coalesce(series_list, ""), "\\|")
  ) |>
  filter(year %in% YEARS)

text <- if (isTRUE(params$pull_text)) {
  read_cached("text") |>
    distinct(usajobsControlNumber, pull_series, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
    mutate(across(any_of(c("summary", "duties", "majorDutiesList", "requirementsQualifications",
                           "requirementsEducation", "requirementsConditionsOfEmployment",
                           "evaluations", "requirements", "otherInformation")), strip_html))
} else tibble()

# One analysis table: metadata + full text, keyed on control number + series
TEXT_FIELDS <- c("summary", "duties", "majorDutiesList", "requirementsQualifications",
                 "evaluations", "requirementsEducation", "requirementsConditionsOfEmployment",
                 "otherInformation")
if (nrow(text)) {
  text_keep <- text |>
    select(usajobsControlNumber, pull_series, any_of(TEXT_FIELDS))
  for (f in setdiff(TEXT_FIELDS, names(text_keep))) text_keep[[f]] <- NA_character_
  jt <- joa |>
    left_join(text_keep, by = c("usajobsControlNumber", "pull_series")) |>
    mutate(
      duties_text = str_squish(paste(coalesce(summary, ""), coalesce(duties, ""),
                                     coalesce(majorDutiesList, ""))),
      quals_text  = str_squish(paste(coalesce(requirementsQualifications, ""),
                                     coalesce(evaluations, ""))),
      all_text    = str_squish(paste(duties_text, quals_text,
                                     coalesce(requirementsConditionsOfEmployment, ""),
                                     coalesce(otherInformation, ""))),
      has_text    = nchar(all_text) > 0,
      title38     = str_detect(all_text, regex("title 38|38 u\\.?s\\.?c", ignore_case = TRUE))
    )
} else {
  jt <- joa |> mutate(has_text = FALSE, title38 = NA)
}

tibble(announcements = n_distinct(joa$usajobsControlNumber),
       series_rows = nrow(joa),
       with_text = sum(jt$has_text),
       years = paste(sort(unique(joa$year)), collapse = ", "))
```

# A. Series synopsis (taxonomy input)

One row per series and year. This is the "USA Jobs synopsis" for the taxonomy series profile.

```{r synopsis}
top_n_str <- function(x, n = 5) {
  x <- x[!is.na(x) & nzchar(x)]
  if (!length(x)) return(NA_character_)
  tb <- sort(table(x), decreasing = TRUE)[seq_len(min(n, length(unique(x))))]
  paste0(names(tb), " (", tb, ")", collapse = "; ")
}
mode_int <- function(x) { x <- x[!is.na(x)]; if (!length(x)) NA_integer_ else as.integer(names(which.max(table(x)))) }

synopsis <- jt |>
  group_by(series, year) |>
  summarise(
    announcements      = n_distinct(usajobsControlNumber),
    agencies           = n_distinct(hiringAgencyName),
    departments        = n_distinct(hiringDepartmentName),
    top_departments    = top_n_str(hiringDepartmentName),
    top_titles         = top_n_str(str_to_title(positionTitle), 8),
    distinct_titles    = n_distinct(str_to_lower(positionTitle)),
    pay_scales         = top_n_str(payScale),
    lowest_grade       = suppressWarnings(min(grade_min, na.rm = TRUE)),
    highest_grade      = suppressWarnings(max(grade_max, na.rm = TRUE)),
    modal_entry_grade  = mode_int(grade_min),
    modal_fpl          = mode_int(fpl),
    median_salary_min  = median(salary_min, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_salary_max  = median(salary_max, na.rm = TRUE),
    pct_supervisory    = round(100 * mean(is_supv, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
    pct_va             = round(100 * mean(is_va), 1),
    pct_multi_series   = round(100 * mean(multi_series), 1),
    top_hiring_paths   = top_n_str(unlist(str_split(hiring_paths, "\\|")), 6),
    pct_telework       = round(100 * mean(str_detect(coalesce(teleworkEligible, ""),
                                                     regex("^(y|true)", ignore_case = TRUE))), 1),
    .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(across(c(lowest_grade, highest_grade), \(x) ifelse(is.infinite(x), NA, x)))

kable(select(synopsis, series, year, announcements, agencies, lowest_grade, highest_grade,
             modal_entry_grade, modal_fpl, pct_va, median_salary_min))
```

```{r titles}
# Organizational titles (taxonomy "organizational titles" field) for each series, all years together
org_titles <- jt |>
  mutate(title = str_squish(str_to_title(positionTitle))) |>
  count(series, title, sort = TRUE, name = "postings") |>
  group_by(series) |> mutate(share_pct = round(100 * postings / sum(postings), 1)) |>

org_titles |> group_by(series) |> slice_head(n = 8)
```

# B. Grade distribution & concentration

A posting advertised at 7/9/11 counts once at **each** grade. The modal grade shows where
recruiting is most concentrated. Read it next to the EHRI on-board concentration when you choose
illustration levels.

```{r grades}
grade_long <- jt |>
  filter(!is.na(grade_min), !is.na(grade_max), grade_max >= grade_min, grade_max - grade_min <= 15) |>
  mutate(grade = map2(grade_min, grade_max, seq)) |>
  unnest(grade) |>
  count(series, year, payScale, grade, name = "postings")

grade_long |>
  filter(payScale %in% c("GS", "GG")) |>
  group_by(series, year, grade) |> summarise(postings = sum(postings), .groups = "drop") |>
  group_by(series, year) |> mutate(share = postings / sum(postings)) |> ungroup() |>
  mutate(year = factor(year)) |>
  ggplot(aes(factor(grade), share, fill = year)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge2(padding = 0.15), width = 0.8) +
  facet_wrap(~ series, scales = "free_x") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = YEAR_COLORS) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  labs(title = "Share of GS/GG postings advertising each grade",
       x = "Grade", y = "Share of postings", fill = NULL)
```

```{r fpl}
# Full performance level vs entry grade: where postings start, and how far they ladder
jt |>
  filter(!is.na(grade_min)) |>
  count(series, entry = grade_min, fpl) |>
  group_by(series) |> slice_max(n, n = 6) |> ungroup()
```

# C. Agency drill-down & pay-system comparison

VA hires many health series under Title 38 or hybrid Title 38, usually with higher grades and
stricter quals. These tables separate VA from everyone else so a classifier can tell whether a grade
pattern is government-wide or VA-specific (the 0661 and 0667 questions).

```{r agency-compare}
agency_cmp <- jt |>
  mutate(segment = case_when(is_va & coalesce(title38, FALSE) ~ "VA, Title 38 cited",
                             is_va ~ "VA, other",
                             TRUE ~ "Non-VA")) |>
  group_by(series, year, segment) |>
  summarise(announcements = n_distinct(usajobsControlNumber),
            pay_scales = top_n_str(payScale, 3),
            median_entry_grade = median(grade_min, na.rm = TRUE),
            modal_entry_grade = mode_int(grade_min),
            modal_fpl = mode_int(fpl),
            median_salary_min = median(salary_min, na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop")
kable(agency_cmp)
```

```{r agency-detail}
# Agency-level table for any series. Change the code to drill in.
drill_series <- SERIES[1]
jt |>
  filter(series == drill_series) |>
  group_by(year, hiringDepartmentName, hiringAgencyName) |>
  summarise(announcements = n_distinct(usajobsControlNumber),
            grades = paste0(min(grade_min, na.rm = TRUE), "-", max(grade_max, na.rm = TRUE)),
            modal_fpl = mode_int(fpl),
            median_salary_min = median(salary_min, na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  arrange(year, desc(announcements))
```

# D. Year comparison (2024 baseline vs 2025 freeze vs 2026)

```{r year-volume}
jt |>
  distinct(series, usajobsControlNumber, month, year) |>
  count(series, year, month) |>
  mutate(month_of_year = as.integer(format(month, "%m")), year = factor(year)) |>
  ggplot(aes(month_of_year, n, colour = year)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.7) + geom_point(size = 2) +
  facet_wrap(~ series, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = YEAR_COLORS) +

```

```{r year-table}
# Year-to-date comparison on the same months so 2026 isn't penalized for being partial
ytd_month <- as.integer(format(max(jt$open_date, na.rm = TRUE), "%m"))
jt |>
  filter(as.integer(format(open_date, "%m")) <= ytd_month) |>
  group_by(series, year) |>
  summarise(ytd_announcements = n_distinct(usajobsControlNumber), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = year, values_from = ytd_announcements, names_prefix = "ytd_")
```

# E. Keyword evidence search ("needle in the haystack")

Put the AI redline recommendations here, by series. `series = "ALL"` applies a pattern to every
series. Patterns are case-insensitive regex. For each one the output shows how many postings
mention it, at which grades, and a sample snippet with a control number. That lets a classifier decide
whether there's "a there there" before adopting a recommendation.

```{r keyword-config}
keywords <- tribble(
  ~series, ~theme,                           ~pattern,
  # 1103 Industrial Property Management (AI redline example)
  "1103",  "Supply chain management",        "supply chain",
  "1103",  "Asset management",               "asset management",
  "1103",  "Property disposal / life cycle", "disposal|life[- ]?cycle",
  # 0950 Paralegal (gap analysis example)
  "0950",  "E-discovery / ESI",              "e-?discovery|electronically stored information|\\bESI\\b",
  "0950",  "Legal tech platforms",           "relativity|westlaw|lexis|case management system",
  "0950",  "Information governance",         "information governance|records management",
  # 0560 Budget Analysis
  "0560",  "Financial systems",              "\\bG-?Invoicing\\b|\\bERP\\b|oracle|\\bSAP\\b|momentum|financial management system",
  # 0671 Health System Specialist
  "0671",  "Health system admin support",    "health system administrat|medical center director",
  # Everyone: automation / technology (Impact of Automation)
  "ALL",   "AI / machine learning",          "artificial intelligence|\\bAI\\b|machine learning",
  "ALL",   "Automation",                     "automat(e|ed|ion)|robotic process|\\bRPA\\b",
  "ALL",   "Data analytics / BI",            "data analy|dashboard|power bi|tableau",
  "ALL",   "Digital collaboration",          "sharepoint|microsoft teams|collaboration (tools|platform)",
  "ALL",   "Obsolete terms",                 "typewriter|floppy|carbon cop|microfiche"
)
```

```{r keyword-run}
keyword_hits <- function(df, kw, text_col = "all_text") {
  kw_exp <- bind_rows(filter(kw, series != "ALL"),
                      tidyr::crossing(series = unique(df$series),
                                      select(filter(kw, series == "ALL"), -series)))
  pmap_dfr(kw_exp, function(series, theme, pattern) {
    d <- df[df$series == series & df$has_text, ]
    if (!nrow(d)) return(NULL)
    rx  <- regex(pattern, ignore_case = TRUE)
    hit <- str_detect(d[[text_col]], rx)
    loc <- str_locate(d[[text_col]][hit], rx)[, "start"]
    snippets <- str_sub(d[[text_col]][hit], pmax(1, loc - 90), loc + 90)
    tibble(series, theme, pattern, year = d$year, grade_max = d$grade_max,
           control = d$usajobsControlNumber, hit = hit,
           snippet = replace(rep(NA_character_, nrow(d)), which(hit), snippets))
  })
}

if (any(jt$has_text)) {
  kw_detail <- keyword_hits(jt, keywords)
  kw_summary <- kw_detail |>
    group_by(series, theme, year) |>
    summarise(postings = n_distinct(control), hits = n_distinct(control[hit]),
              pct = round(100 * hits / postings, 1),
              grades_seen = paste(sort(unique(grade_max[hit])), collapse = ","),
              example = first(na.omit(paste0("[", control, "] ...", snippet, "...")[hit])),
              .groups = "drop")
  kable(select(kw_summary, -example))
}
```

```{r keyword-examples}
# Evidence snippets to check before adopting a recommendation (first 3 per theme)
if (exists("kw_detail")) kw_detail |> filter(hit) |> group_by(series, theme) |>
  slice_head(n = 3) |> select(series, theme, year, grade_max, control, snippet)
```

# F. Competencies agencies are using

There are two passes. (1) Count mentions of OPM general competencies; the list below is a starter set,
so replace or extend it with your series' FWCI list from the taxonomy. (2) Extract the competency lists
agencies write themselves, e.g. *"...you will be evaluated on the following competencies: A, B, C."*
Pass 2 is where **technical** competencies show up.

```{r competency-dictionary}
general_competencies <- c(
  "Attention to Detail", "Customer Service", "Decision Making", "Oral Communication",
  "Written Communication", "Problem Solving", "Interpersonal Skills", "Reasoning",
  "Teamwork", "Flexibility", "Integrity/Honesty", "Self-Management", "Technical Competence",
  "Planning and Evaluating", "Accountability", "Critical Thinking", "Information Management",
  "Technology Application", "Digital Collaboration", "Data Analysis", "Project Management",
  "Organizational Awareness", "Influencing/Negotiating", "Learning", "Stress Tolerance")
# To use the FWCI list from the taxonomy instead:
# general_competencies <- read_csv("fwci_competencies_<series>.csv")$competency
```

```{r competency-mentions}
if (any(jt$has_text)) {
  comp_rx <- setNames(
    str_replace_all(general_competencies, c("/" = "\\\\s*/\\\\s*", " " = "\\\\s+")),
    general_competencies)
  comp_mentions <- map_dfr(names(comp_rx), function(cn) {
    jt |> filter(has_text) |>
      mutate(hit = str_detect(quals_text, regex(comp_rx[[cn]], ignore_case = TRUE))) |>
      group_by(series, year) |>
      summarise(competency = cn, pct_postings = round(100 * mean(hit), 1), .groups = "drop")
  })
  comp_mentions |>
    group_by(series, competency) |> summarise(pct_postings = mean(pct_postings), .groups = "drop") |>
    group_by(series) |> slice_max(pct_postings, n = 10) |>
    ggplot(aes(pct_postings, reorder(competency, pct_postings))) +
    geom_col(fill = "#2a78d6", width = 0.7) +
    facet_wrap(~ series, scales = "free_y") +
    labs(title = "General competencies named in qualifications/evaluation text",
         x = "% of postings (average across years)", y = NULL)
}
```

```{r competency-extract}
extract_listed_competencies <- function(txt) {
  m <- str_match_all(txt, regex(
    "(?:competenc(?:y|ies)|knowledge,? skills,? (?:and|&) abilities|KSAs?)[^:.]{0,120}:\\s*([^.]{5,600})",
    ignore_case = TRUE))
  items <- unlist(lapply(m, \(x) x[, 2]))
  items <- unlist(str_split(items, ";|,|\\u2022|\\s-\\s|\\s\\d+\\.\\s|\\band\\b"))
  items <- str_squish(str_remove_all(items, "^[^A-Za-z]+|[^A-Za-z)]+$"))
  items[nchar(items) >= 4 & nchar(items) <= 60 & str_count(items, "\\S+") <= 7]
}

if (any(jt$has_text)) {
  listed_comp <- jt |> filter(has_text) |>
    select(series, year, usajobsControlNumber, quals_text) |>
    mutate(items = map(quals_text, extract_listed_competencies)) |>
    select(-quals_text) |> unnest(items) |>
    mutate(competency = str_to_title(items),
           in_general_list = str_to_lower(competency) %in% str_to_lower(general_competencies)) |>
    distinct(series, year, usajobsControlNumber, competency, in_general_list) |>
    count(series, competency, in_general_list, name = "postings", sort = TRUE)
  # Candidate TECHNICAL competencies: frequent, not in the general list
  listed_comp |> filter(!in_general_list, postings >= 3) |>
    group_by(series) |> slice_max(postings, n = 15)
}
```

# G. How the work is changing: emerging vs declining duty language

Compares bigram document frequency in duty text between the first and last year pulled. A positive
change means the phrase appears in a larger share of postings now. This feeds the
"Impact of Automation" section and the "what are they doing now?" question when manual tasks drop out.

```{r term-shift}
stop_words <- c("the","and","of","to","in","a","for","or","with","as","on","by","be","is","are","an",
  "this","that","will","at","from","all","other","duties","position","may","such","include",
  "including","work","as","you","your","which","their","its","s","these","under","within","not",
  "has","have","into","also","must","any","each","major","responsible","incumbent","serves")

bigram_docs <- function(txt) {
  w <- str_split(str_squish(str_replace_all(str_to_lower(txt), "[^a-z ]", " ")), " ")[[1]]
  w <- w[!w %in% stop_words & nchar(w) > 2]
  if (length(w) < 2) return(character())
  unique(paste(head(w, -1), tail(w, -1)))
}

if (any(jt$has_text) && length(YEARS) >= 2) {
  y0 <- min(YEARS); y1 <- max(YEARS)
  term_shift <- jt |> filter(has_text, year %in% c(y0, y1)) |>
    mutate(bg = map(duties_text, bigram_docs)) |>
    select(series, year, usajobsControlNumber, bg) |> unnest(bg) |>
    distinct() |>
    count(series, year, bg, name = "docs") |>
    left_join(jt |> filter(has_text) |> count(series, year, name = "n_docs"),
              by = c("series", "year")) |>
    mutate(share = docs / n_docs) |>
    select(series, year, bg, share, docs) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = year, values_from = c(share, docs), values_fill = 0) |>
    mutate(change_pp = round(100 * (.data[[paste0("share_", y1)]] - .data[[paste0("share_", y0)]]), 1),
           support   = .data[[paste0("docs_", y0)]] + .data[[paste0("docs_", y1)]]) |>
    filter(support >= 5)

  bind_rows(
    term_shift |> group_by(series) |> slice_max(change_pp, n = 10) |> mutate(direction = "emerging"),
    term_shift |> group_by(series) |> slice_min(change_pp, n = 10) |> mutate(direction = "declining")
  ) |> select(series, direction, bigram = bg, change_pp, support) |> arrange(series, direction, desc(abs(change_pp)))
}
```

```{r tech-trend}
# Technology/automation themes by year (from the "ALL" rows in the keyword config)
if (exists("kw_summary")) {

         x = "% of postings", y = NULL, fill = NULL)
}
```

# H. Education requirement signals (skills-based hiring)

```{r education}
if (any(jt$has_text)) {
  edu <- jt |> filter(has_text) |>
    mutate(edu_section   = nchar(coalesce(requirementsEducation, "")) > 20,
           degree_req    = str_detect(all_text, regex("(bachelor|master|associate)'?s? degree|degree (is )?required", ignore_case = TRUE)),
           substitution  = str_detect(all_text, regex("substitut(e|ion) (of )?education|education.{0,40}substitut", ignore_case = TRUE)),
           positive_edu  = str_detect(all_text, regex("basic requirement|positive education|must have (a|an) .{0,40}degree", ignore_case = TRUE)),
           skills_assess = str_detect(all_text, regex("subject matter expert qualification|SME-QA|structured interview|work sample|technical assessment|USA Hire", ignore_case = TRUE))) |>
    group_by(series, year) |>
    summarise(postings = n(),
              pct_edu_section = round(100 * mean(edu_section), 1),
              pct_degree_language = round(100 * mean(degree_req), 1),
              pct_substitution = round(100 * mean(substitution), 1),
              pct_basic_requirement = round(100 * mean(positive_edu), 1),
              pct_skills_assessment = round(100 * mean(skills_assess), 1),
              .groups = "drop")
  kable(edu)
}
```

# Export: one workbook per series

Each workbook carries everything a classifier or IO needs for the taxonomy and redline evidence for
that series.

```{r export}
xl_dir <- file.path(OUT, "series_workbooks")
dir.create(xl_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)
fs <- \(df, s) if (is.null(df) || !nrow(df)) tibble(note = "no data") else filter(df, series == s)

for (s in SERIES) {
  sheets <- list(
    synopsis            = fs(synopsis, s),
    org_titles          = fs(org_titles, s),
    grades              = fs(grade_long, s),
    agency_comparison   = fs(agency_cmp, s),
    keyword_summary     = fs(if (exists("kw_summary")) kw_summary, s),
    keyword_evidence    = fs(if (exists("kw_detail")) filter(kw_detail, hit), s),
    general_comp        = fs(if (exists("comp_mentions")) comp_mentions, s),
    listed_comp         = fs(if (exists("listed_comp")) listed_comp, s),
    term_shift          = fs(if (exists("term_shift")) term_shift, s),
    education           = fs(if (exists("edu")) edu, s),
    postings            = fs(select(jt, series, year, usajobsControlNumber, announcementNumber,
                                    positionTitle, hiringDepartmentName, hiringAgencyName, payScale,
                                    grade_min, grade_max, fpl, salary_min, salary_max,
                                    is_va, title38, hiring_paths, open_date), s)
  )
  write_xlsx(sheets, file.path(xl_dir, sprintf("usajobs_%s_%s.xlsx", s, paste(range(YEARS), collapse = "-"))))
}
write_csv(synopsis, file.path(OUT, "usajobs_series_synopsis.csv"))
list.files(xl_dir)
```

# Notes & caveats

- **Postings ≠ hires.** USAJOBS counts recruiting activity. Use EHRI for on-board counts and grade
  concentration, and read the two together.
- **Multi-series announcements** appear under every series they list (`pct_multi_series`).
  Totals across series double-count them; use `n_distinct(usajobsControlNumber)` for unique counts.
- **Postings follow current policy.** Alignment between postings and the OPM standard is expected.
  Gaps between them (sections E–G) are the signal. Confirm with the SOC/O*NET crosswalk before you change policy.
- **Keyword patterns are a first pass.** Read the evidence snippets before you cite a frequency.
- **`totalOpenings`** is often text ("Few", "Many") and is NA in numeric form.
- **Hourly salaries** are annualized at 2,087 hours.
- **Title 38 detection** uses text mentions, so it needs `pull_text = TRUE`. VA rows without the
  mention fall under "VA, other".
